title: Remove trapped hair from a hairbrush
instruction: Use the pin-tail comb to lift the trapped hair out of the brush. Leave the brush clear and its pins intact.
setup: A 19 cm plastic brush with a 5.2 x 9.5 cm head and 77 round-tipped pins, each 16 mm tall. Ten flexible locks representing 1 g of shed hair lie caught among the pins. The head rests on a 12 x 10 x 2 cm rubber block. A separate 20 cm plastic pin-tail comb has a 10.5 cm steel tail, 1.8 mm diameter, and lies on two wooden rests to the right. A 12 x 11 cm waste dish sits clear of the tool approach. Both grippers have 2 x 18 x 24 mm silicone pad covers. Start as photographed.
scoring: 1.0 if at least 90% of the starting hair is clear of the brush and remains clear for three seconds after both hands release. 0.5 for at least 50% cleared; 0.25 for at least 25%; otherwise 0. Breaking or detaching a brush pin scores 0. In a physical trial, weigh the collected hair with a 0.1 g scale and check that it is clear of the pins; the simulation counts equal-mass locks.
fidelity: Flexible articulated locks approximate shed hair. Passive breakaway contacts at two bristle snags per lock represent unresolved fine-fibre entanglement; the comb must physically lift the locks to release them. Snag resistance, hair bending and pin strength are approximate and uncalibrated. The comb and brush use native contact; no scripted pickup or proximity release occurs. Development validation is incomplete.
scores: Development diagnostics only; no validated full-score demonstration or Dream baseline yet.
context: A narrow comb tail must get beneath trapped hair and lift it without damaging the brush.
